exercises.name: Dumbbell Bench Press
exercises.summary: The friendliest chest press for a comeback — each arm works on its own.
exercises.video_title: Dumbbell Bench Press Tutorial – Proper Form and Technique
instructions: Sit on a flat bench with a dumbbell on each thigh, then lie back and use your legs to help lift them to your shoulders.
Set your feet flat, squeeze your shoulder blades together, and press the dumbbells up until your arms are almost straight.
Lower under control until your elbows are just below the bench, elbows tucked to about 45 degrees.
Press back up and stop just short of locking out to keep tension on the chest.
form_tips: Keep your wrists stacked over your elbows the whole way.
Drive your feet into the floor for a stable base.
Pick a weight you can control for 10 smooth reps in week one.
common_mistakes: Flaring the elbows straight out to the sides.
Bouncing the dumbbells off the chest.
Arching the lower back off the bench to move heavier weight.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Shoulder Press
exercises.summary: Press overhead to rebuild pressing strength and shoulder stability.
exercises.video_title: Standing Dumbbell Shoulder Press (Tutorial + Tips)
instructions: Sit tall (or stand) holding a dumbbell just outside each shoulder, palms facing forward.
Brace your core and tuck your ribs so you are not leaning back.
Press the dumbbells up and slightly together until your arms are straight.
Lower under control until the dumbbells are back level with your ears.
form_tips: Keep elbows slightly in front of the body, not flared wide.
Squeeze your glutes to stop your lower back arching.
Start seated with back support while you rebuild the pattern.
common_mistakes: Turning the press into a backward lean / standing incline press.
Only pressing halfway up.
Letting the dumbbells drift forward away from the shoulders.

exercises.name: One-Arm Dumbbell Row
exercises.summary: A supported back row that builds pulling strength and posture.
exercises.video_title: Single-Arm Dumbbell Row on a Bench: Perfect Form Tutorial
instructions: Put one knee and the same-side hand on a bench, other foot on the floor.
Let the dumbbell hang straight down with a flat back, roughly parallel to the floor.
Pull the dumbbell to the side of your ribcage, leading with your elbow.
Pause, squeeze your shoulder blade, then lower all the way down.
form_tips: Keep your back flat and hips square to the floor.
Think 'elbow to ceiling', not 'lift with the hand'.
Move slowly — no jerking or twisting the torso.
common_mistakes: Rounding the upper back at the bottom.
Rotating the torso to heave the weight up.
Shrugging the shoulder toward the ear instead of rowing.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Romanian Deadlift
exercises.summary: A hip hinge that teaches you to load the hamstrings safely.
exercises.video_title: How to do a Dumbbell Romanian Deadlift | Proper Form | NASM
instructions: Stand holding a dumbbell in front of each thigh, knees softly bent.
Push your hips straight back and let the dumbbells slide down the front of your legs.
Stop when you feel a strong hamstring stretch, back still flat, around knee height.
Drive your hips forward to stand tall and squeeze your glutes at the top.
form_tips: Keep the dumbbells close — almost brushing your legs.
The movement is hips going back, not the torso folding down.
Keep a long, neutral spine from head to hips.
common_mistakes: Rounding the lower back to reach lower.
Turning it into a squat by bending the knees a lot.
Going too heavy before the hinge pattern feels natural.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Goblet Squat
exercises.summary: The best first squat back — the front load keeps you upright and honest.
exercises.video_title: Goblet Squat Tutorial – Proper Form and Technique
instructions: Hold one dumbbell vertically against your chest, cupping the top end with both hands.
Stand with feet a little wider than shoulders, toes slightly out.
Sit down between your legs, keeping your chest tall and heels planted.
Push through the whole foot to stand back up, squeezing your glutes.
form_tips: Keep your elbows inside your knees at the bottom.
Aim for thighs at least parallel if your mobility allows.
Brace your core as if about to be poked in the stomach.
common_mistakes: Heels lifting off the floor.
Knees caving inward on the way up.
Leaning forward so the dumbbell drifts away from the chest.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Lateral Raise
exercises.summary: An isolation move for wider, healthier-feeling shoulders.
exercises.video_title: How to Do Dumbbell Lateral Raises | Proper Form & Technique
instructions: Stand tall with a light dumbbell in each hand at your sides, slight bend in the elbows.
Lead with your elbows and raise the dumbbells out to the sides.
Stop when your arms are level with your shoulders.
Lower slowly back to your sides with control.
form_tips: Keep your thumbs level with or slightly above your pinkies.
Use a weight light enough that you never swing.
Keep your shoulders down away from your ears.
common_mistakes: Using momentum from the hips to fling the weight up.
Shrugging so the traps take over.
Raising the arms far above shoulder height.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Biceps Curl
exercises.summary: The classic arm builder — simple, and easy to progress week to week.
exercises.video_title: Standing Dumbbell Bicep Curl | Proper Technique + Form Tips
instructions: Stand tall with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing forward.
Keeping your upper arms pinned to your sides, curl the dumbbells toward your shoulders.
Squeeze the biceps at the top for a beat.
Lower slowly until your arms are fully straight.
form_tips: Keep your elbows still — only the forearms move.
Control the lowering phase; it builds as much as the lift.
Stand still: no rocking or leaning back.
common_mistakes: Swinging the torso to start the rep.
Letting the elbows drift forward into a partial front raise.
Cutting the range short at the bottom.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Hammer Curl
exercises.summary: A neutral-grip curl that is kinder to the wrists and elbows.
exercises.video_title: Dumbbell Hammer Curls Tutorial | Perfect Technique
instructions: Stand with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing your thighs (neutral grip).
Keep your upper arms locked at your sides and curl the dumbbells up.
Stop when your wrists are just above your elbows, then squeeze.
Lower under control for a two to three count.
form_tips: Keep the wrists straight and firm — don't let them bend.
No swinging: pick a weight you can strictly control.
Keep shoulders back and down throughout.
common_mistakes: Letting the elbows flare out to the sides.
Shrugging the shoulders up to help.
Dropping the weight quickly instead of lowering it.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Walking Lunge
exercises.summary: A single-leg builder for balance, control, and everyday strength.
exercises.video_title: Walking Lunge Tutorial – Proper Form and Technique
instructions: Stand tall with a dumbbell in each hand at your sides, core braced.
Step forward into a lunge, bending both knees to about 90 degrees.
Stop just before your back knee touches the floor.
Drive through your front foot to stand, then step through with the other leg.
form_tips: Keep your chest up and torso tall the whole way.
Take a stride long enough that your front shin stays near vertical.
Go slow and controlled — this is a balance exercise too.
common_mistakes: Front knee collapsing inward.
Leaning the torso forward over the front leg.
Rushing the steps and losing balance.

exercises.name: Barbell Back Squat
exercises.summary: The foundational lower-body strength lift. Rebuild it slowly.
exercises.video_title: How to Barbell Back Squat | A Tutorial for Beginners
instructions: Set the bar on your upper traps in the rack, hands just outside the shoulders.
Un-rack, step back into a stance slightly wider than your shoulders, toes a little out.
Brace your core, sit your hips down and back until your thighs are at least parallel.
Drive through your whole foot to stand, keeping your chest up.
form_tips: Start with just the empty bar for a week to relearn the groove.
Keep your knees tracking out over your toes.
Always squat in a rack with the safety pins set.
common_mistakes: Knees caving inward as you stand up.
Rounding the lower back at the bottom.
Coming up onto the toes / heels lifting.

exercises.name: Barbell Front Squat
exercises.summary: A front-loaded squat that hammers the quads and demands an upright torso.
exercises.video_title: Barbell Front Squat Tutorial
instructions: Rest the bar on the front of your shoulders, elbows high, fingers loosely under the bar.
Un-rack and step back into a shoulder-width stance.
Keeping your elbows up and torso tall, sit straight down.
Drive up through your midfoot without letting the elbows drop.
form_tips: Elbows high is the whole game — point them at the far wall.
Only the fingertips need to be under the bar; it rests on the shoulders.
Build wrist and shoulder mobility first if the rack position pinches.
common_mistakes: Elbows dropping, which dumps the bar forward.
Rounding forward out of the bottom.
Loading it heavy before the rack position is comfortable.

exercises.name: Barbell Bench Press
exercises.summary: The main horizontal press for upper-body strength.
exercises.video_title: Barbell Bench Press Tutorial – Proper Form and Technique
instructions: Lie back with eyes under the bar, feet flat, shoulder blades pinched together.
Grip a little wider than shoulder width and un-rack to straight arms.
Lower the bar under control to the base of your sternum, elbows about 45 degrees.
Press back up and slightly toward the rack until arms are straight.
form_tips: Use a spotter or work inside a rack with safety arms.
Keep your wrists straight, bar over the forearm bones.
Keep your shoulder blades tucked and 'set' the entire set.
common_mistakes: Bouncing the bar off the chest.
Elbows flaring to 90 degrees, stressing the shoulders.
Hips lifting off the bench to grind a rep.

exercises.name: Barbell Deadlift
exercises.summary: A total-body pull. Technique first, load much later.
exercises.video_title: Barbell Deadlift Tutorial – Proper Form and Technique
instructions: Stand with mid-foot under the bar, shins an inch away, feet hip-width.
Hinge down and grip the bar just outside your legs.
Drop your hips, lift your chest, and pull the slack out of the bar.
Push the floor away and stand tall, keeping the bar dragging up your legs.
form_tips: Brace hard before every rep, like bracing for a punch.
Keep the bar in contact with your legs the whole way.
Reset your setup between every rep rather than bouncing.
common_mistakes: Rounding the lower back as you break the floor.
Hips shooting up first, turning it into a stiff-leg pull.
Jerking the bar off the floor instead of a smooth pull.

exercises.name: Barbell Romanian Deadlift
exercises.summary: A top-down hip hinge that builds strong, resilient hamstrings.
exercises.video_title: Barbell Deadlift & Hinge Tutorial – Proper Form
instructions: Start standing tall holding the bar at your hips, knees softly bent.
Push your hips back and lower the bar down the front of your thighs.
Stop at a strong hamstring stretch, roughly just below the knee, back flat.
Drive the hips forward to return to standing and squeeze the glutes.
form_tips: Keep the bar touching your legs the whole range.
Knees stay in a fixed soft bend — they don't keep bending.
Think 'push the hips to the wall behind you'.
common_mistakes: Letting the bar drift away from the body.
Rounding the back to chase more depth.
Bending the knees more to reach the floor (that's a deadlift).

exercises.name: Barbell Bent-Over Row
exercises.summary: A heavy horizontal pull to balance out all that pressing.
exercises.video_title: Barbell Bent Over Row Tutorial – Proper Form and Technique
instructions: Hold the bar with an overhand grip just outside your knees.
Hinge forward to roughly 45 degrees with a flat back, knees bent.
Pull the bar to your lower ribs / upper stomach, elbows close to the body.
Lower under control until your arms are straight.
form_tips: Lock your torso angle in place — it should not rise as you pull.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the top.
Keep your neck neutral, eyes on the floor a few feet ahead.
common_mistakes: Standing up with each rep to heave the weight.
Rounding the back.
Using a stance so upright it becomes a shrug.

exercises.name: Barbell Overhead Press
exercises.summary: Standing press for real overhead strength and a solid core.
exercises.video_title: Standing Barbell Press Tutorial – Proper Form and Technique
instructions: Un-rack the bar onto the front of your shoulders, hands just outside shoulder width.
Stand with feet hip-width, squeeze glutes, brace the core.
Press the bar straight up, moving your head back slightly to clear a path.
Once past your forehead, push your head 'through' and lock out overhead.
form_tips: Keep the bar over your mid-foot — a vertical bar path.
Squeeze your glutes to stop the lower back arching.
Finish with the bar stacked over your ears, not in front.
common_mistakes: Leaning back into a standing incline press.
Pressing the bar around your face instead of moving the head.
Not finishing the lockout fully overhead.

exercises.name: Barbell Hip Thrust
exercises.summary: The most direct glute builder — easy to load and easy to feel.
exercises.video_title: Hip Thrust Tutorial – Proper Form and Technique
instructions: Sit on the floor with your upper back against a bench, a padded bar over your hips.
Plant your feet flat, shins vertical at the top of the movement.
Drive through your heels and push your hips up until your body is flat from knees to shoulders.
Squeeze your glutes hard at the top, then lower with control.
form_tips: Tuck your chin and keep your ribs down — don't arch the back to finish.
Push the floor away through your heels.
Pause for a beat at the top of every rep.
common_mistakes: Over-arching the lower back instead of squeezing the glutes.
Feet too far forward so the hamstrings take over.
Only pushing halfway up.

exercises.name: Kettlebell Swing
exercises.summary: Explosive hip power and conditioning in one short, brutal set.
exercises.video_title: Kettlebell Swings Tutorial – Proper Form and Technique
instructions: Stand a foot behind the bell, feet shoulder-width, and hinge to grip it with both hands.
Hike the bell back between your legs like a football snap.
Snap your hips forward hard to float the bell to about chest height.
Let it swing back down, catching it with another hip hinge, and repeat.
form_tips: The power is a hip snap, not a squat and not an arm lift.
Keep your arms relaxed — they're just ropes.
Finish each rep standing tall with glutes and abs braced.
common_mistakes: Squatting the bell up and down.
Lifting with the shoulders/arms.
Letting the bell drop too low and rounding the back.

exercises.name: Kettlebell Goblet Squat
exercises.summary: Same great first squat as the dumbbell version — the handle just sits nicer.
exercises.video_title: Goblet Squats – Kettlebell for Beginners
instructions: Hold the kettlebell by the horns of the handle, close against your chest.
Set feet slightly wider than shoulders, toes turned out a little.
Sit straight down between your legs, elbows brushing the inside of your knees.
Stand back up by pushing the floor away, staying tall.
form_tips: Keep the bell glued to your chest the whole rep.
Keep your weight balanced over your mid-foot.
Brace your core before you descend.
common_mistakes: Letting the chest fall forward.
Heels rising off the floor.
Knees caving in as you stand.

exercises.name: Kettlebell Deadlift
exercises.summary: The safest way to learn the hinge and the deadlift pattern.
exercises.video_title: Kettlebell Deadlift Tutorial – Proper Form and Technique
instructions: Stand over the bell with feet hip-width, bell between your arches.
Push your hips back and hinge down to grip the handle with both hands.
Flatten your back, take a breath, and brace.
Stand up by driving your hips forward, then hinge back down to place it.
form_tips: Arms stay straight — they're just hooks.
Keep the bell close to your body on the way up and down.
Finish tall with a glute squeeze, no back arch.
common_mistakes: Rounding the back to reach the handle.
Squatting the weight up instead of hinging.
Yanking the bell off the floor.

exercises.name: Kettlebell Clean
exercises.summary: Gets the bell to your shoulder to start presses and squats.
exercises.video_title: How to Do the Kettlebell Clean (Step-by-Step for Beginners)
instructions: Start with the bell on the floor slightly outside one foot.
Hinge, grip it with one hand, and hike it back between your legs.
Snap the hips and guide the bell up close to your body, elbow tucking in.
Let the bell 'roll' around the wrist into the racked position at your shoulder — don't let it flip and bang.
form_tips: Keep the bell close, like zipping up a jacket.
Loosen your grip as the bell comes up so it rotates smoothly.
Practice with a light bell until the catch is soft.
common_mistakes: Letting the bell arc far out then crash onto the forearm.
Gripping too hard so the bell flips over the hand.
Using the arm to curl the bell up instead of the hips.

exercises.name: Kettlebell Overhead Press
exercises.summary: A single-arm press — the offset load makes your core work hard.
exercises.video_title: The Correct Form for Kettlebell Overhead Press
instructions: Start with the kettlebell racked at one shoulder, bell resting on the back of the forearm.
Stand tall with ribs stacked over hips and glutes squeezed.
Press the bell straight up until your arm is fully locked out, biceps by your ear.
Lower under control back to the racked position.
form_tips: Keep your wrist neutral and straight under the bell.
Brace your core hard — the weight is trying to bend you sideways.
Keep the elbow tucked as you start the press.
common_mistakes: Leaning away from the bell to press it up.
Letting the wrist bend back under the load.
Not locking out fully at the top.

exercises.name: Turkish Get-Up
exercises.summary: A slow, full-body stability drill. Master it light — it's worth it.
exercises.video_title: The Turkish Get Up (step by step)
instructions: Lie on your back, press a light bell up with one arm, same-side knee bent.
Roll up onto your free elbow, then your hand, keeping the bell locked overhead.
Bridge your hips up and sweep your straight leg back into a half-kneeling position.
Stand up, then reverse every step slowly to return to the floor.
form_tips: Keep your eyes on the bell until you are standing.
Practice with a shoe balanced on your fist before you add weight.
Move one deliberate step at a time — there is no rush.
common_mistakes: Rushing and losing the vertical arm.
Skipping the elbow-then-hand sequence.
Starting too heavy before the pattern is grooved.

exercises.name: Push-Up
exercises.summary: A whole upper body and core in one move, anywhere, no gear.
exercises.video_title: How to do a Push-Up | Proper Form & Technique | NASM
instructions: Start in a plank with hands a little wider than your shoulders, body in a straight line.
Brace your core and squeeze your glutes.
Bend your elbows to about 45 degrees and lower until your chest is just off the floor.
Push the floor away to return to the top.
form_tips: Keep a straight line from head to heels — no sagging hips.
Move your chest and hips together as one unit.
If full range is too hard, raise your hands (see Incline Push-Up).
common_mistakes: Hips sagging toward the floor.
Only doing a partial range at the top.
Elbows flaring straight out to 90 degrees.

exercises.name: Incline Push-Up
exercises.summary: A push-up with your hands raised — the perfect week-one starting point.
exercises.video_title: How to do an Incline Push-Up | Proper Form & Technique | NASM
instructions: Place your hands on a sturdy bench, table, or wall, a bit wider than your shoulders.
Step your feet back so your body forms a straight, leaning line.
Lower your chest toward the surface with elbows about 45 degrees.
Press back up to straight arms.
form_tips: The higher the surface, the easier — lower it as you get stronger.
Keep your body rigid from head to heels.
Full range beats big numbers with a short range.
common_mistakes: Letting the hips pike up or sag down.
Choosing a wobbly surface.
Rushing reps instead of controlling the lower.

exercises.name: Bodyweight Squat
exercises.summary: Rebuild the squat pattern with zero load before you add weight.
exercises.video_title: Bodyweight Squat Tutorial – Proper Form and Technique
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, toes slightly turned out.
Reach your arms forward as a counterbalance.
Sit your hips down and back, keeping your heels down and chest tall.
Descend as far as you comfortably can, then stand back up.
form_tips: Push your knees out in line with your toes.
Keep your weight spread across the whole foot.
Only go as deep as you can keep a flat back.
common_mistakes: Heels lifting off the floor.
Knees caving inward.
Rounding the lower back at the bottom.

exercises.name: Bodyweight Walking Lunge
exercises.summary: Single-leg strength and balance with no equipment needed.
exercises.video_title: Walking Lunge Exercise Tutorial – Proper Form and Technique
instructions: Stand tall with your hands on your hips or by your sides.
Step forward and bend both knees toward 90 degrees.
Keep your front shin near vertical and torso upright.
Push through the front foot to stand, then step through with the other leg.
form_tips: Look ahead, not down, to help your balance.
Control the descent — don't drop into the bottom.
Hold a wall lightly at first if balance is shaky.
common_mistakes: Front knee sliding far past the toes.
Torso pitching forward.
Back knee slamming into the floor.

exercises.name: Front Plank
exercises.summary: Teach your core to stay stiff and protect your spine.
exercises.video_title: How to do a Plank | Proper Form & Technique | NASM
instructions: Set your forearms on the floor with elbows directly under your shoulders.
Step your feet back so your body is a straight line from head to heels.
Squeeze your glutes and pull your belly button toward your spine.
Hold for time, breathing steadily, then rest.
form_tips: Keep your hips level with your shoulders — no sagging or piking.
Look at the floor to keep your neck neutral.
Stop the set when your form breaks, not when you're exhausted.
common_mistakes: Hips sagging toward the floor.
Butt piking up into an inverted V.
Holding your breath.

exercises.name: Side Plank
exercises.summary: Builds the side-core strength that keeps your torso from tipping.
exercises.video_title: Side Plank Tutorial – Proper Form and Technique
instructions: Lie on your side with your elbow under your shoulder and legs stacked.
Lift your hips until your body is a straight line from head to feet.
Squeeze your glutes and brace your core.
Hold for time, then switch sides.
form_tips: Stack your shoulder directly over your elbow.
Keep your hips pushed forward, not rolling back.
Drop to a bent-knee version if the full hold is too much.
common_mistakes: Hips sagging toward the floor.
Rotating the chest toward the ground.
Elbow placed ahead of the shoulder.

exercises.name: Glute Bridge
exercises.summary: Wake up glutes that have been sitting dormant at a desk.
exercises.video_title: Glute Bridge Tutorial – Proper Form and Technique
instructions: Lie on your back, knees bent, feet flat and about hip-width apart.
Tuck your ribs down and press your lower back lightly into the floor.
Drive through your heels and lift your hips until your body is flat from knees to shoulders.
Squeeze your glutes at the top, then lower with control.
form_tips: Push the movement with your glutes, not your lower back.
Keep a straight line — don't over-arch at the top.
Pause and squeeze for a beat on every rep.
common_mistakes: Arching the lower back to finish the rep.
Pushing through the toes instead of the heels.
Feet too far away so the hamstrings cramp.

exercises.name: Bird Dog
exercises.summary: A gentle anti-rotation drill that builds a stable, pain-resistant back.
exercises.video_title: How to do a Bird Dog | Proper Form & Technique | NASM
instructions: Start on all fours, hands under shoulders and knees under hips.
Brace your core so your spine is neutral.
Reach one arm forward and the opposite leg back until both are level with your torso.
Return under control and switch sides.
form_tips: Keep your hips level — imagine balancing a glass of water on your lower back.
Move slowly; the control is the point.
Only reach as far as you can without twisting.
common_mistakes: Rotating the hips as the leg lifts.
Lifting the leg higher than the torso and arching the back.
Rushing through reps.

exercises.name: Dead Bug
exercises.summary: Teaches your core to stay braced while your arms and legs move.
exercises.video_title: How to do a Dead Bug | Proper Form & Technique | NASM
instructions: Lie on your back with arms reaching at the ceiling and knees stacked over hips, bent 90 degrees.
Press your lower back flat into the floor and hold it there.
Slowly lower one arm overhead and the opposite leg toward the floor.
Return to the start and switch sides, keeping the back flat the whole time.
form_tips: Exhale as you extend the arm and leg.
Only go as far as you can keep your lower back pinned down.
Keep the movement slow and quiet.
common_mistakes: Lower back arching up off the floor.
Holding your breath.
Moving fast and losing the brace.

exercises.name: Mountain Climbers
exercises.summary: A simple cardio burst you can add to the end of any session.
exercises.video_title: Mountain Climber Tutorial – Proper Form and Technique
instructions: Start in a strong push-up plank, wrists under shoulders.
Keep a straight line from head to heels and brace your core.
Drive one knee toward your chest, then switch legs.
Continue alternating at a controlled, steady pace.
form_tips: Keep your hips low and level — don't let them bounce up.
Move the legs straight in and out, not side to side.
Start slow; speed can come later.
common_mistakes: Hips piking up toward the ceiling.
Rounding the upper back.
Going so fast that form falls apart.

exercises.name: Band Pull-Apart
exercises.summary: A 60-second posture and shoulder-health fix. Do it every session.
exercises.video_title: Resistance Band Pull Apart
instructions: Hold a light band in front of you at shoulder height, hands a bit wider than shoulders.
Keep your arms straight and elbows locked.
Pull the band apart until your arms form a T, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Return slowly to the start with control.
form_tips: Keep your ribs down and shoulders away from your ears.
Pinch your shoulder blades like you're holding a pencil between them.
Use a band light enough to keep the arms straight.
common_mistakes: Bending the elbows to cheat the range.
Shrugging the shoulders up.
Letting the band snap back quickly.

exercises.name: Band Bent-Over Row
exercises.summary: A joint-friendly back row you can do anywhere with one band.
exercises.video_title: Band Bent Over Row – Proper Form & Technique
instructions: Stand on the middle of the band, feet shoulder-width, a handle in each hand.
Hinge forward to about 45 degrees with a flat back and braced core.
Pull the handles to your lower ribs, leading with your elbows.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together, then extend the arms with control.
form_tips: Keep your torso angle fixed — don't stand up as you pull.
Keep elbows close to your sides.
Step wider on the band for more resistance.
common_mistakes: Rounding the back.
Using the legs and back to jerk the handles up.
Shrugging instead of rowing.

exercises.name: Band Chest Press
exercises.summary: A pressing option with constant tension and no bench needed.
exercises.video_title: How To: Standing Resistance Band Chest Press
instructions: Anchor the band behind you at chest height (a door anchor works well).
Face away, a handle in each hand at chest level, elbows bent, one foot forward for balance.
Press your hands forward until your arms are almost straight.
Return slowly, keeping tension, until your hands are back by your chest.
form_tips: Keep your shoulders down and back the whole time.
Don't lock the elbows hard at the end — keep a soft bend.
Step further forward to increase the resistance.
common_mistakes: Arching the back to push harder.
Letting the elbows drop below shoulder height.
Rushing the return and losing tension.

exercises.name: Band Squat
exercises.summary: Adds gentle load to the squat pattern — great for home days.
exercises.video_title: How To: Resistance Band Squat
instructions: Stand on the middle of a loop band, feet shoulder-width apart.
Bring the top of the band up to your shoulders, elbows up.
Sit your hips down and back, keeping your chest tall and heels down.
Drive through your feet to stand, pushing your knees out against the band.
form_tips: Let the band cue your knees to track outward.
Keep the tension by not fully relaxing at the top.
Use a heavier band or a wider stance for more challenge.
common_mistakes: Knees caving in despite the band.
Heels lifting.
Leaning the chest forward.

exercises.name: Band Lateral Walk
exercises.summary: Fires up the side-glutes that stabilise your knees and hips.
exercises.video_title: Lateral Walk Tutorial – Proper Form and Technique
instructions: Loop a mini band around your legs just above the knees (or ankles for more).
Set a quarter-squat stance: knees bent, hips back, chest up.
Step sideways, leading with one foot and keeping tension on the band.
Follow with the other foot but never let your feet come closer than hip-width.
form_tips: Keep your toes pointing forward the whole time.
Stay low — don't bob up and down as you step.
Take small, controlled steps.
common_mistakes: Standing up tall between steps.
Letting the trailing foot snap in and kill the tension.
Feet turning out to the sides.

exercises.name: Band Face Pull
exercises.summary: The best single move for undoing desk posture and cranky shoulders.
exercises.video_title: Banded Face Pulls Tutorial – Proper Form and Technique
instructions: Anchor a band at about face height and hold one end in each hand.
Step back until there's tension, arms straight out in front, thumbs pointing back.
Pull the band toward your face, splitting your hands apart as you go.
Lead with high elbows and squeeze the rear delts, then return slowly.
form_tips: Keep your elbows at or above shoulder height.
Don't jut your head forward to meet the band.
Pause and squeeze at the end of each rep.
common_mistakes: Using a band so heavy the elbows drop.
Turning it into a straight row to the chest.
Leaning back and using bodyweight instead of the upper back.

exercises.name: Band Biceps Curl
exercises.summary: Constant-tension curls that are easy on the elbows.
exercises.video_title: Bicep Curl (bands) | Technique and 3 Most Common Mistakes
instructions: Stand on the middle of the band with a handle in each hand, palms forward.
Keep your elbows pinned to your sides.
Curl the handles up toward your shoulders, squeezing the biceps.
Lower slowly until your arms are straight, keeping tension.
form_tips: Keep your wrists straight and your elbows still.
Stand on more of the band for extra resistance.
Control the lowering — don't let the band yank your arms down.
common_mistakes: Elbows drifting forward.
Leaning back to start the curl.
Letting the band snap back at the bottom.

exercises.name: Leg Press
exercises.summary: Load the legs safely without needing balance or a spotter.
exercises.video_title: Leg Press Tutorial
instructions: Sit back into the machine with your feet shoulder-width on the platform, mid-foot.
Extend your legs to lift the sled and release the safety handles.
Lower the platform under control until your knees reach about 90 degrees.
Press back up through your whole foot without snapping the knees straight.
form_tips: Keep your lower back and hips flat against the pad.
Don't let your knees cave inward.
Leave a soft bend in the knees at the top.
common_mistakes: Lowering so far your hips curl up off the seat.
Locking the knees hard at the top.
Placing hands on the knees during the press.

exercises.name: Leg Extension
exercises.summary: Isolates the quads — handy for rebuilding after knee-shy time off.
exercises.video_title: How to do the Leg Extension properly (in 80 seconds)
instructions: Adjust the seat so your knees line up with the machine's pivot point.
Set the shin pad just above your ankles and hold the handles.
Straighten your legs smoothly, squeezing the quads at the top.
Lower under control; don't let the weight stack slam.
form_tips: Keep your back against the pad and don't bounce.
Pause briefly at full extension.
Start light — this move can feel intense on the knees.
common_mistakes: Swinging the torso to fling the weight up.
Seat set wrong so the knee sits ahead of the pivot.
Dropping the weight quickly on the way down.

exercises.name: Seated Leg Curl
exercises.summary: Direct hamstring work to balance all the quad and glute training.
exercises.video_title: Beginner's Guide: Seated Leg Curl
instructions: Sit with your back flat against the pad and the leg pad resting on your lower shins.
Lower the thigh pad so it's snug just above your knees.
Curl your heels down and under toward the seat, squeezing the hamstrings.
Return slowly to straight legs without letting the stack crash.
form_tips: Keep your torso still — only the knees bend.
Squeeze for a beat at the bottom of the curl.
Keep your feet in a neutral position, toes relaxed.
common_mistakes: Lifting the hips off the seat to get more range.
Using momentum instead of a controlled curl.
Setting the thigh pad too loose so your legs lift out.

exercises.name: Chest Press Machine
exercises.summary: A guided press so you can push a little without a spotter.
exercises.video_title: Chest Press Machine Tutorial | Beginner's Guide to Gym Machines
instructions: Set the seat so the handles line up with the middle of your chest.
Sit back with your shoulder blades pinched and feet flat.
Press the handles forward until your arms are almost straight.
Return slowly until your hands are back level with your chest.
form_tips: Keep your back against the pad — don't lunge forward off it.
Keep wrists straight and elbows a touch below the shoulders.
Stop just short of a hard lockout.
common_mistakes: Seat too low, turning it into a shoulder press.
Shrugging the shoulders up to the ears.
Letting the weight stack bang between reps.

exercises.name: Lat Pulldown
exercises.summary: Build the pulling strength that leads toward your first pull-up.
exercises.video_title: Beginner's Guide: Lat Pulldown
instructions: Set the thigh pad snug and grip the bar a bit wider than shoulder width.
Sit tall with a slight backward lean and your chest up.
Pull the bar to the top of your chest, driving your elbows down and back.
Return slowly until your arms are fully straight and your shoulders stretch up.
form_tips: Start the pull by dropping your shoulder blades down.
Keep the lean slight and fixed — don't row with your whole body.
Bring the bar to your collarbone, not behind your neck.
common_mistakes: Using a big backward swing to yank the bar down.
Pulling the bar behind the neck.
Only doing a half rep and never fully straightening the arms.

exercises.name: Seated Row Machine
exercises.summary: Chest-supported rowing — all back, no lower-back strain.
exercises.video_title: Seated Cable Row Tutorial: Build a Strong Back with Proper Form
instructions: Set the chest pad so you can reach the handles with straight arms.
Sit tall with your chest against the pad and feet planted.
Pull the handles to your torso, driving your elbows straight back.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together, then extend the arms with control.
form_tips: Keep your chest on the pad the whole set.
Think about pulling with your elbows, not your hands.
Pause and squeeze at the end of each pull.
common_mistakes: Leaning back off the pad to move more weight.
Rounding the shoulders forward at the start.
Rushing the return.

exercises.name: Shoulder Press Machine
exercises.summary: Overhead pressing on rails — a safe way back to pressing weight.
exercises.video_title: Shoulder Press Machine | Proper Technique + Form Tips
instructions: Set the seat so the handles start at about shoulder height.
Sit back with your back flat against the pad, feet planted.
Press the handles straight up until your arms are nearly straight.
Lower under control back to shoulder height.
form_tips: Keep your ribs down — don't arch off the backrest.
Keep your head in a neutral position, not craned forward.
Choose a neutral grip if it feels better on the shoulders.
common_mistakes: Seat too high or low, changing the press angle awkwardly.
Arching the lower back to finish the press.
Partial reps that never reach a full lockout.

exercises.name: Seated Cable Row
exercises.summary: Smooth, constant-tension rowing for a stronger back and better posture.
exercises.video_title: Seated Cable Row – Proper Form & Technique
instructions: Sit with a slight knee bend, feet on the platform, and grab the handle.
Sit tall with a flat back and arms extended, feeling a stretch in your back.
Pull the handle to your stomach, driving your elbows straight back.
Squeeze your shoulder blades, then return slowly to a full stretch.
form_tips: Let your shoulder blades move: stretch forward at the front, squeeze at the back.
Keep the torso mostly still — a tiny lean is fine, a big swing is not.
Keep your chest up and shoulders down.
common_mistakes: Rocking back and forth with the lower back.
Rounding forward to reach at the front.
Yanking with the arms and never using the back.

exercises.name: Cable Chest Fly
exercises.summary: Isolates the chest with tension through the whole range.
exercises.video_title: How to Perform Cable Flys | Proper Form and Tips
instructions: Set both pulleys to around shoulder height and take a handle in each hand.
Step forward into a staggered stance with a slight forward lean.
Keep a fixed soft bend in your elbows and open your arms wide until you feel a chest stretch.
Bring the handles together in front of your chest, squeezing the pecs.
form_tips: Keep the elbow angle locked — it's a fly, not a press.
Lead the movement with your upper arms, not your hands.
Keep your shoulder blades back and down.
common_mistakes: Bending and straightening the elbows (making it a press).
Using too much weight and shrugging the shoulders forward.
Letting the arms go so far back the shoulder gets pinched.

exercises.name: Cable Triceps Pushdown
exercises.summary: Simple, effective triceps work that spares the elbows.
exercises.video_title: Rope Tricep Pushdowns (Tutorial + Tips)
instructions: Attach a rope or bar to a high pulley and grip it with your elbows tucked at your sides.
Stand tall with a slight forward lean and a braced core.
Straighten your arms down, pushing the attachment toward your thighs.
Squeeze the triceps, then return under control to about 90 degrees at the elbow.
form_tips: Keep your elbows pinned to your sides the whole set.
Only the forearms move — the upper arms stay still.
With a rope, spread the ends apart at the bottom.
common_mistakes: Elbows drifting forward so the lats and shoulders take over.
Leaning way over to push with bodyweight.
Short reps that never fully straighten the arms.

exercises.name: Cable Biceps Curl
exercises.summary: Keeps tension on the biceps even at the bottom of the rep.
exercises.video_title: How to: Cable Bicep Curl | Form Tutorial
instructions: Attach a bar to a low pulley and hold it with an underhand, shoulder-width grip.
Stand tall a step back from the machine, elbows at your sides.
Curl the bar up toward your shoulders, keeping your upper arms still.
Squeeze at the top, then lower slowly until your arms are straight.
form_tips: Keep your elbows pinned and your posture upright.
Don't let the weight stack pull your arms behind your body.
Control the lowering phase fully.
common_mistakes: Swinging the torso to start each rep.
Elbows travelling forward and up.
Cutting the bottom of the range short.

exercises.name: Cable Face Pull
exercises.summary: Shoulder-health gold. A few sets a week keeps pressing pain-free.
exercises.video_title: Cable Face Pull (Exercise Library)
instructions: Set a rope at about face height and hold one end in each hand, palms facing in.
Step back until there's tension, arms extended, core braced.
Pull the rope toward your face, separating your hands past your ears.
Keep your elbows high, squeeze the rear delts, then return slowly.
form_tips: Set the pulley at face height, not all the way at the top.
Keep the elbows level with or above the shoulders.
Squeeze the shoulder blades at the end of each rep.
common_mistakes: Letting the elbows drop and turning it into a row.
Jutting the head forward to meet the rope.
Using momentum from the legs and back.

exercises.name: Cable Woodchop
exercises.summary: Trains rotational core power for sport and everyday twisting.
exercises.video_title: Cable Woodchop | Proper Form Tutorial for Core Rotation
instructions: Set the pulley high and grab the handle with both hands, standing side-on.
Set a wide, athletic stance and brace your core.
Pull the handle down and across your body toward the opposite hip, rotating through your trunk.
Return under control to the start, resisting the pull the whole way.
form_tips: Rotate through the ribcage and hips, keeping the arms fairly straight.
Let your back foot pivot as you turn.
Move with control — this is about power, not speed with sloppy form.
common_mistakes: Only using the arms and not rotating the torso.
Rounding or over-arching the lower back.
Going too heavy and getting yanked off balance.

exercises.name: Wall Push-Up
exercises.summary: The gentlest way into pressing — learn the plank line with almost no load.
exercises.video_title: Wall Push-Up
instructions: Stand a foot or two back from a wall, hands on it at shoulder height and width.
Straighten your body into one line from head to heels, core braced.
Bend your elbows to about 45 degrees and bring your chest toward the wall.
Press back to straight arms. Step further from the wall to make it harder.
form_tips: Keep your body rigid — no sagging or piking at the hips.
Move your chest and hips together as one unit.
The further your feet are from the wall, the harder it gets.
common_mistakes: Bending only at the hips instead of the elbows.
Letting the head drop forward.
Standing too close so there's almost no range.

exercises.name: Knee Push-Up
exercises.summary: A full-range push-up from the knees — the bridge to your first floor push-up.
exercises.video_title: How to do a Push-Up (with regressions) | NASM
instructions: Kneel and place your hands a little wider than your shoulders.
Walk your hands forward so your body is a straight line from knees to head.
Lower your chest all the way to the floor, elbows about 45 degrees.
Press back up to straight arms without letting your hips sag.
form_tips: Hips in line with your shoulders — don't pike up.
Go all the way down; full range beats extra reps.
Cross your ankles and lift your feet for a cleaner line.
common_mistakes: Bending at the hips so only the shoulders move.
Half reps at the top.
Hands too far back, under the chest instead of the shoulders.

exercises.name: Decline Push-Up
exercises.summary: Feet elevated shifts the load onto the upper chest and shoulders.
exercises.video_title: How To: Decline Push-Up
instructions: Set up in a push-up position with your feet on a chair, step or low bench.
Hands slightly wider than your shoulders, body in a straight line.
Lower your chest toward the floor, elbows tucked to about 45 degrees.
Press back up, keeping your hips level with your shoulders.
form_tips: The higher the feet, the harder — start low.
Brace your core so your lower back doesn't arch.
Keep your neck neutral, eyes down.
common_mistakes: Hips sagging or piking.
Only lowering halfway.
Feet on something unstable.

exercises.name: Deficit Push-Up
exercises.summary: Hands raised so your chest drops below them — extra range and a loaded stretch.
exercises.video_title: Deficit Push-up Tutorial
instructions: Place each hand on a sturdy raised surface — books, low blocks, or parallettes.
Set a straight body line with hands under your shoulders.
Lower until your chest sinks below the level of your hands.
Press back up to straight arms, staying rigid throughout.
form_tips: Start with a small deficit (2–4 inches) and build up.
Control the bottom — that's the whole point of the move.
Keep the raised surfaces stable and even.
common_mistakes: Bouncing out of the stretched bottom position.
Letting the shoulders shrug up toward the ears.
Hips dropping as you fatigue.

exercises.name: Archer Push-Up
exercises.summary: Most of your weight goes onto one arm while the other stays straight as an outrigger.
exercises.video_title: Archer Push Ups Tutorial With Correct Form
instructions: Start in a push-up with your hands roughly twice shoulder-width apart.
Bend one arm and lean your weight heavily onto it, keeping the other arm straight.
Lower until your chest nears the floor on the working side.
Press back to the centre and repeat on the other side.
form_tips: Lean toward the working arm — don't just go straight up and down.
Keep your body aligned from feet to head.
Use it as a drop-set partner: archer reps, then finish with full push-ups.
common_mistakes: Bending the 'straight' arm and turning it into a wide push-up.
Hips twisting toward the floor.
Not leaning enough, so the load stays split.

exercises.name: Pike Push-Up
exercises.summary: An inverted-V press that turns the push-up into overhead shoulder work.
exercises.video_title: Pike Push Up Tutorial For Beginners (With Progressions)
instructions: From a push-up position, walk your feet in and lift your hips into an upside-down V.
Hands a little wider than shoulders, head between your arms.
Bend your elbows and lower the top of your head toward the floor.
Press back up until your arms are straight.
form_tips: The more vertical your torso, the more it hits the shoulders.
Elevate your feet on a step to make it harder.
Keep your legs as straight as your hamstrings allow.
common_mistakes: Letting the hips drop so it becomes a regular push-up.
Flaring the elbows straight out.
Looking forward instead of keeping the neck neutral.

exercises.name: Band Overhead Press
exercises.summary: Press a band overhead — constant tension, easy on the shoulders, scalable by band.
exercises.video_title: Resistance Band Single Arm Overhead Press
instructions: Stand on the middle of the band, feet hip-width, a handle at each shoulder.
Stack your ribs over your hips and brace your core and glutes.
Press the handles straight up until your arms are fully extended.
Lower under control back to shoulder height.
form_tips: Keep your wrists straight and stacked over your elbows.
Step wider on the band or use a heavier band for more resistance.
Don't lean back — press the band, don't arch around it.
common_mistakes: Turning it into a backward-leaning standing incline press.
Pressing only halfway up.
Letting the band snap the arms down on the way back.

exercises.name: Band Lat Pulldown
exercises.summary: Anchor a band high and pull down — the closest thing to a lat pulldown with no machine.
exercises.video_title: Resistance Band Lat Pulldown
instructions: Anchor a band above head height — a door anchor at the top, or over a sturdy bar.
Kneel or stand tall facing the anchor, an end of the band in each hand, arms overhead.
Pull your elbows down and back toward your ribs, squeezing your shoulder blades.
Return slowly until your arms are fully straight and your shoulders stretch up.
form_tips: Start the pull by dropping your shoulder blades, not by bending the elbows.
Keep a tall spine and a slight backward lean, fixed.
Step back from the anchor for more tension.
common_mistakes: Using a big body swing to yank the band down.
Shrugging the shoulders up at the top.
Half reps that never let the lats stretch.

exercises.name: Band Straight-Arm Pulldown
exercises.summary: A long-lever lat move that also teaches you to brace against a pull.
exercises.video_title: Resistance Band Straight Arm Lat Pulldown (At Home)
instructions: Anchor a band at about chest or head height and face it.
Hold the band with both hands, arms straight out in front, slight elbow bend.
Keeping your arms nearly straight, pull the band down in an arc to your thighs.
Return slowly, resisting the band, and brace so your torso doesn't get pulled forward.
form_tips: Lock a soft elbow bend and keep it fixed the whole rep.
Squeeze your abs to stop your lower back arching.
Feel the lats, not the triceps, doing the work.
common_mistakes: Bending and straightening the elbows (that's a pushdown).
Leaning the whole torso forward and back.
Letting the ribs flare and the back arch.

exercises.name: Split Squat
exercises.summary: A static lunge — both feet stay planted so you can focus on one leg at a time.
exercises.video_title: Split Squat / Static Lunge Tutorial
instructions: Step one foot forward and one back into a stable split stance, torso tall.
Bend both knees straight down until your back knee nearly touches the floor.
Keep your front shin close to vertical and your weight through the front heel.
Drive through the front foot to stand, then finish all reps before switching legs.
form_tips: Both knees bend together — think 'down', not 'forward'.
Keep your front knee tracking over your toes, not caving in.
Hold a wall or chair lightly if your balance is shaky.
common_mistakes: Leaning the torso forward over the front leg.
Front knee sliding far past the toes.
Pushing off the back foot instead of loading the front leg.

exercises.name: Reverse Lunge
exercises.summary: Step back into the lunge — kinder on the knees than a forward lunge and easy to balance.
exercises.video_title: Reverse Lunge Form for Beginners (Step-by-Step)
instructions: Stand tall, then take a controlled step straight back with one foot.
Lower until both knees are bent about 90 degrees, back knee near the floor.
Keep your torso upright and your weight on the front foot.
Drive through the front heel to step back to standing, then alternate.
form_tips: Step back far enough that your front shin stays near vertical.
Look ahead, not down, for balance.
Lower with control — don't drop the back knee onto the floor.
common_mistakes: Short step so the front knee jams forward.
Torso pitching forward.
Front knee caving inward on the way up.

exercises.name: Bulgarian Split Squat
exercises.summary: Back foot elevated — one of the hardest things you can do to a leg with no equipment.
exercises.video_title: Bulgarian Split Squat Tutorial (Proper Technique & Form)
instructions: Stand a stride in front of a bench or chair; rest the top of your back foot on it.
Set your front foot far enough forward that the knee stays over the mid-foot.
Lower straight down until your back knee is just off the floor.
Drive through the front foot to stand. Finish all reps, then switch.
form_tips: A slight forward torso lean biases the glute; staying vertical biases the quad.
Keep the front heel planted the whole time.
Hold a doorframe lightly for balance while you learn it.
common_mistakes: Front foot too close, so the knee shoots forward and the heel lifts.
Pushing off the back foot instead of loading the front leg.
Losing balance and rushing the reps.

exercises.name: Cossack Squat
exercises.summary: A deep side-to-side squat that builds single-leg strength and hip mobility together.
exercises.video_title: Cossack Squat Tutorial & Progressions
instructions: Stand with your feet well wider than your shoulders, toes slightly out.
Shift your weight onto one leg and sit down into it, keeping that heel planted.
Let the other leg straighten, toes up, as you descend as far as your hips allow.
Push back to the centre and shift to the other side.
form_tips: Keep your chest lifted and core tight so your back doesn't round.
Only go as deep as you can control — depth comes with practice.
Hold your hands out front or a light support as a counterweight.
common_mistakes: Bending-leg heel lifting off the floor.
Rounding the back to reach lower.
Knee caving inward on the working leg.

exercises.name: Box Pistol Squat
exercises.summary: A single-leg squat down to a box or chair — the doorway to a full pistol.
exercises.video_title: How to: Box Pistol Squat
instructions: Stand in front of a box or chair, balancing on one leg, other leg extended forward.
Sit your hips back and down under control until you touch the box.
Keep the free leg and both arms reaching forward as a counterweight.
Stand back up through the working heel without pushing off the box.
form_tips: Use a higher box to regress, lower to progress.
Keep the working heel flat — elevate it slightly if your ankles are tight.
Touch the box lightly; don't crash and rebound.
common_mistakes: Dropping onto the box and bouncing up.
Heel lifting off the floor.
Knee caving in as you stand.

exercises.name: Pistol Squat
exercises.summary: A full-depth squat on one leg — the benchmark for lower-body strength without weights.
exercises.video_title: How to Get Your First PISTOL SQUAT (Step-by-Step Progression)
instructions: Balance on one leg with the other extended straight in front, arms forward.
Sit back and down slowly, keeping the working heel flat and chest up.
Descend until the back of your thigh meets your calf.
Drive straight back up without letting the free foot touch down.
form_tips: Slow eccentrics (5s down to a box) build the strength to stand back up.
Hold a light band or doorframe for assistance while you develop it.
Keep the extended leg as straight and high as your mobility allows.
common_mistakes: Heel popping up and the weight shifting to the toes.
Knee collapsing inward under load.
Falling backward at the bottom instead of controlling the descent.

exercises.name: Wall Sit
exercises.summary: An isometric quad burner you can do anywhere — hold time is the progression.
exercises.video_title: Wall Sit | Proper Form Tutorial for Leg Endurance
instructions: Stand with your back flat against a wall, feet about hip-width and a step forward.
Slide down the wall until your thighs are parallel to the floor.
Knees stacked over your ankles, weight in your heels.
Hold for time, breathing steadily, then slide back up.
form_tips: Aim for a 90-degree bend at the knees and hips.
Keep your whole back in contact with the wall.
Progress by adding 5–10 seconds each week.
common_mistakes: Knees drifting past the toes (feet too close to the wall).
Weight on the toes instead of the heels.
Holding your breath.

exercises.name: Band Good Morning
exercises.summary: A standing hip hinge loaded across the shoulders by a band — teaches the RDL pattern safely.
exercises.video_title: How To Do Banded Good Mornings
instructions: Stand on the middle of a band, feet shoulder-width, and loop the top over the back of your shoulders.
Soften your knees and brace your core.
Push your hips straight back, letting your torso hinge forward with a flat back.
Stop at a strong hamstring stretch, then drive your hips forward to stand tall.
form_tips: Hips travel back, not the chest folding down.
Keep a fixed soft knee bend — the knees don't keep bending.
Keep the band settled on muscle, not on your neck.
common_mistakes: Rounding the lower back to reach further.
Turning it into a squat by bending the knees.
Standing on too little band so there's no resistance.

exercises.name: Band Pull-Through
exercises.summary: The workhorse loaded hip hinge for band training — all glute, no lower-back strain.
exercises.video_title: Banded Pull Through | Movement Demo
instructions: Anchor a band low behind you; face away and pass the band between your legs, a handle in each hand.
Step forward until there's tension, feet a little wider than hip-width.
Hinge your hips back with a flat back, hands sliding down between your thighs.
Snap your hips forward and squeeze your glutes to stand tall.
form_tips: Keep your shins near vertical so the glutes do the work, not the quads.
Arms stay long like straps — don't row the band with your arms.
Finish standing tall with ribs down, not leaning back.
common_mistakes: Squatting the weight up instead of hinging.
Bending the elbows and turning it into a row.
Over-arching the lower back at the top.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Romanian Deadlift
exercises.summary: A one-legged hip hinge that builds hamstring strength, balance and symmetry at once.
exercises.video_title: How to Perform Single Leg Romanian Deadlifts | Bodyweight Tutorial
instructions: Stand on one leg with a soft knee bend, hips square, spine long.
Hinge at the hip, reaching your free leg straight back in line with your torso.
Lower until you feel a strong hamstring stretch or your torso is near parallel.
Drive the standing hip forward to return to tall, squeezing the glute.
form_tips: Move slowly — this is a balance exercise as much as a strength one.
Keep your hips level; don't let the back hip open to the ceiling.
Touch a wall or chair with one hand while you build the balance.
common_mistakes: Rounding the back to reach the floor.
Twisting the hips open instead of staying square.
Bending the standing knee like a squat.

exercises.name: Hollow Body Hold
exercises.summary: The gymnastics core position — full-body tension with your lower back glued to the floor.
exercises.video_title: Hollow Body Hold | Proper Form Tutorial for Core Stability
instructions: Lie on your back, press your lower back flat into the floor and hold it there.
Lift your shoulder blades and head slightly off the floor.
Raise your straight legs a few inches, arms reaching past your head.
Hold this dish shape, breathing shallowly. Bend the knees or drop the arms to regress.
form_tips: Lower back pressed down is the one rule that matters.
The lower your arms and legs, the harder — raise them to make it easier.
Start with 10–20 second holds and build up.
common_mistakes: Lower back arching up off the floor.
Holding your breath and tensing the neck.
Legs so low the back pops up.

exercises.name: Superman / Prone Back Raise
exercises.summary: Trains the whole back of the body to hold you upright — a counter to all that sitting.
exercises.video_title: Superman - Back extension
instructions: Lie face down, arms extended past your head, legs straight.
Brace your glutes and gently lift your arms, chest and legs a few inches off the floor.
For a back-row feel, pull your elbows down toward your ribs and squeeze your shoulder blades.
Hold briefly, then lower with control.
form_tips: Lift with a gentle range — this is not a max spinal extension.
Keep your neck long; look at the floor, not forward.
Squeeze the glutes to share the load with the lower back.
common_mistakes: Cranking the neck up and back.
Jerking into the top position.
Over-extending the lower back instead of a small, controlled lift.

exercises.name: Band Pallof Press
exercises.summary: Press a band straight out while it tries to twist you — pure anti-rotation core strength.
exercises.video_title: Banded Pallof Press | Proper Form Tutorial for Core Stability
instructions: Anchor a band at chest height and stand side-on to it, both hands holding the end at your sternum.
Set a shoulder-width stance, brace your core, ribs down.
Press the band straight out in front of you and resist its pull to rotate you.
Hold for a beat, then bring it back to your chest. Finish reps, then face the other way.
form_tips: Move slowly — the anti-rotation is the exercise.
Step further from the anchor for more challenge.
Keep your hips and shoulders square to the front the whole time.
common_mistakes: Letting the band twist your torso toward the anchor.
Pressing with the shoulders shrugged.
Holding your breath instead of bracing and breathing.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Calf Raise
exercises.summary: Full-range calf work on one leg — bodyweight is plenty of load here.
exercises.video_title: Single Leg Calf Raise Exercise Tutorial - Proper Form and Technique
instructions: Stand on the ball of one foot on the edge of a step, holding a wall for balance.
Let your heel drop below the step for a full stretch.
Press up onto your toes as high as you can and pause at the top.
Lower slowly back into the stretch. Finish reps, then switch legs.
form_tips: Full range: deep stretch at the bottom, high squeeze at the top.
Use the wall only for balance, not to take weight.
Keep the working knee straight but not locked.
common_mistakes: Tiny bouncy reps with no real range.
Rolling onto the outside of the foot.
Rushing the lowering phase.

exercises.name: Burpee
exercises.summary: The classic full-body conditioning move — scale it down to a step-back, up to a jump.
exercises.video_title: Burpees for Beginners (STEP BY STEP GUIDE!)
instructions: From standing, squat down and place your hands on the floor.
Step or jump your feet back into a plank (add a push-up here to make it harder).
Step or jump your feet back up to your hands.
Stand up — add a jump with the hands overhead for the full version.
form_tips: Beginner: step back and step in, no jump, hands on a chair.
Keep a flat back in the plank position — don't let the hips sag.
Land softly through the whole foot on the jump.
common_mistakes: Sagging or piking the hips in the plank.
Landing stiff-legged from the jump.
Going so fast the form falls apart.

exercises.name: Skater Hops
exercises.summary: Lateral bounds that build single-leg power, ankle and knee stability, and a bit of cardio.
exercises.video_title: Speed Skaters Exercise (Skater Hops): Proper Form
instructions: Start balanced on one leg with a slight knee and hip bend.
Push off sideways and bound onto the other foot, swinging the trailing leg behind.
Land softly on a bent leg and pause until you're balanced.
Bound back the other way. Slow and controlled beats fast and sloppy.
form_tips: Land soft — absorb the hop through the hip, knee and ankle.
Don't let the landing knee cave inward.
Use your arms for balance and momentum.
common_mistakes: Landing stiff-legged.
Knee collapsing in on landing.
Rushing so you never actually balance between hops.

exercises.name: Diamond Push-Up
exercises.summary: Hands together under your chest — the same push-up, far more triceps.
exercises.video_title: Close Grip / Diamond Push-Up | Proper Form Tutorial
instructions: Set up in a plank and bring your hands together so thumbs and index fingers form a triangle.
Keep your body in a straight line and your elbows tucked close to your ribs.
Lower until your chest touches your hands, then press back up.
form_tips: Elbows brush your sides — don't let them flare.
Regress to knees or an incline if your wrists complain.
Full range: chest to hands every rep.
common_mistakes: Elbows flaring out to the sides.
Hips sagging as the triceps tire.
Only doing a half rep.

exercises.name: Wide Push-Up
exercises.summary: Hands wide to bias the chest and get a deeper stretch each rep.
exercises.video_title: Wide Push-Up Tutorial
instructions: Place your hands noticeably wider than your shoulders.
Keep a straight body line and brace your core.
Lower with control until your chest nears the floor, then press up.
form_tips: Retract your shoulder blades as you descend.
Don't go so wide that your shoulders feel pinched.
Keep the hips level with the shoulders throughout.
common_mistakes: Hips sagging or piking.
Elbows flaring to a hard 90 degrees.
Going so wide it stresses the shoulder joint.

exercises.name: Spiderman Push-Up
exercises.summary: A push-up with a knee-to-elbow drive — chest, core and hips in one move.
exercises.video_title: Spider-Man Push Up Tutorial
instructions: Start in a strong push-up position, body in a straight line.
As you lower, drive one knee up toward the same-side elbow.
As you press back up, return the foot to the start. Alternate sides.
form_tips: Keep your hips level — don't let them rotate toward the floor.
The knee should arrive by the bottom of the push-up.
Move slowly; the coordination is the challenge.
common_mistakes: Hips twisting as the knee comes up.
Rushing so the push-up range gets short.
Letting the back arch.

exercises.name: Clap Push-Up
exercises.summary: An explosive push-up where your hands leave the floor — builds pressing power.
exercises.video_title: How to do a Plyometric Push-Up | NASM
instructions: Lower into a push-up with your body rigid, arms forming an arrow, not a T.
Press up as explosively as you can so your hands leave the floor.
Clap, then land on soft elbows and immediately absorb into the next rep.
form_tips: Only attempt this once you can do 20+ clean push-ups.
Land with bent elbows to absorb force.
Keep the body a rigid plank the whole time.
common_mistakes: Piking the hips to get airtime.
Landing on locked-out elbows.
Losing the straight body line mid-air.

exercises.name: Band Floor Press
exercises.summary: A lying press with a band around your back — pressing strength with no bench, no floor push-up.
exercises.video_title: How To Do: Resistance Band Floor Press
instructions: Lie on your back, knees bent, and pass a band under your upper back, an end in each hand.
Start with elbows on the floor at about 45 degrees, hands above your chest.
Press the band straight up until your arms are almost straight, then lower under control.
form_tips: Keep your lower back flat — don't arch to press harder.
Control the lowering phase; that's where the muscle works.
Choke up on the band or use a heavier band for more resistance.
common_mistakes: Arching the back off the floor.
Flaring the elbows to a hard 90 degrees.
Letting the band yank the arms down.

exercises.name: Band Pullover
exercises.summary: A lying lat move that also opens up the shoulders and ribcage.
exercises.video_title: Pullover with a Resistance Band
instructions: Anchor a band low behind your head (or hold it taut) and lie on your back, knees bent.
Hold the band with straight arms reaching back overhead.
Keeping the arms nearly straight, pull the band in an arc toward your thighs.
Return slowly to the overhead stretch.
form_tips: Lock a soft elbow bend and keep it fixed.
Keep your ribs down so the back doesn't arch.
Feel the lats, not the shoulders, doing the work.
common_mistakes: Bending and straightening the elbows.
Flaring the ribs and arching the lower back.
Going so far overhead the shoulders pinch.

exercises.name: Band Seated Row
exercises.summary: Sit down, loop the band around your feet, and row — a back builder with zero setup.
exercises.video_title: How To: Resistance Band Seated Row
instructions: Sit tall with legs extended, a band looped around the arches of your feet, an end in each hand.
Start with arms straight and a slight forward reach of the shoulder blades.
Drive your elbows back close to your body, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Return slowly to a full stretch.
form_tips: Keep your chest up and back flat — no rounding.
Pull with the elbows, not the hands.
Sit further back or double the band for more tension.
common_mistakes: Rounding the shoulders forward at the start.
Leaning way back to move the band.
Shrugging instead of rowing.

exercises.name: Band Reverse Fly
exercises.summary: Isolates the rear delts — a small move with a big effect on posture.
exercises.video_title: How To: Resistance Band Reverse Fly
instructions: Hold a band in front of you at shoulder height, an end in each hand, palms down.
Set a slight bend in your elbows and keep it fixed.
Pull your hands apart and back until your arms form a wide T, squeezing the shoulder blades.
Return slowly with control.
form_tips: Keep your shoulders down, away from your ears.
Lead with the pinky side of the hand.
Use a light band — form beats tension here.
common_mistakes: Bending the elbows to cheat the range.
Shrugging the traps up.
Arching the lower back to lean into it.

exercises.name: Band Arnold Press
exercises.summary: An overhead press with a rotation — hits all three heads of the shoulder.
exercises.video_title: Band Arnold Press
instructions: Stand on the band, start with hands in front of your shoulders, palms facing you, elbows down.
As you press up, rotate your palms to face forward.
Finish with arms straight overhead, then reverse the rotation on the way down.
form_tips: Keep your core braced and ribs down — don't lean back.
Rotate smoothly through the middle of the press.
Keep the wrists stacked over the elbows at lockout.
common_mistakes: Leaning back to press the band up.
Rushing the rotation.
Shrugging the shoulders at the top.

exercises.name: Wall Walk
exercises.summary: Walk your feet up a wall into a handstand hold — the bridge to overhead bodyweight strength.
exercises.video_title: The Complete Handstand Guide | From Absolute Beginner
instructions: Start in a push-up position with your feet against the base of a wall.
Walk your hands toward the wall as your feet climb up it.
Go as vertical as you can control, hold briefly, then walk back down.
form_tips: Keep your arms locked straight the whole time.
Only go as high as you can come back down under control.
Squeeze your ribs and glutes so you don't over-arch.
common_mistakes: Bending the elbows and collapsing.
Over-arching the lower back near vertical.
Rushing up with no plan to get down.

exercises.name: Prisoner Squat
exercises.summary: A bodyweight squat with hands behind your head — forces an upright, strong torso.
exercises.video_title: How to do a Prisoner Squat | Proper Form & Technique | NASM
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder-width, toes slightly out, fingers laced behind your head.
Pull your elbows back to open your chest.
Sit your hips down and back to at least parallel, keeping your torso tall.
Drive through your whole foot to stand.
form_tips: Keep your elbows wide and chest proud the whole rep.
Push your knees out in line with your toes.
Keep your weight through the mid-foot.
common_mistakes: Elbows collapsing forward.
Chest falling toward the floor.
Heels lifting.

exercises.name: Sumo Squat
exercises.summary: A wide-stance squat that brings the inner thighs and glutes into the party.
exercises.video_title: The Squat You NEED To Be Doing! (Sumo Squat)
instructions: Stand with your feet well wider than shoulder-width, toes turned out about 30 degrees.
Keep your chest up and core braced.
Sit straight down, knees tracking over your toes, until your thighs are parallel.
Drive up through your heels and squeeze your glutes at the top.
form_tips: Point your knees the same direction as your toes.
Keep your torso as upright as you can.
Push the floor apart with your feet as you stand.
common_mistakes: Knees caving inward.
Leaning the chest forward.
Feet too narrow to feel the inner thighs.

exercises.name: Jump Squat
exercises.summary: An explosive squat that trains power and gets your heart rate up fast.
exercises.video_title: How to do a Squat Jump | Proper Form & Technique | NASM
instructions: Start in a shoulder-width stance and drop into a quarter-to-half squat.
Explode up, extending hips, knees and ankles, and swing your arms for momentum.
Land softly through the whole foot and immediately absorb into the next squat.
form_tips: Land quiet — soft knees and hips absorb the force.
Keep your chest up on both the jump and the landing.
Warm up your legs first; this is high-impact.
common_mistakes: Landing stiff-legged.
Knees caving in on the landing.
Rounding forward as you jump.

exercises.name: Shrimp Squat
exercises.summary: A single-leg squat where you hold your back foot — a pistol alternative with a different balance demand.
exercises.video_title: Shrimp Squat | Tutorial & Progressions
instructions: Stand on one leg, bend the other knee and hold that foot behind you with the same-side hand.
Sit down slowly, keeping the standing heel flat and chest tall.
Lower until your back knee lightly touches the floor, then drive back up.
form_tips: Reach your free arm forward as a counterweight.
Regress by lowering to a stack of books or a low box.
Keep the working knee tracking over the toes.
common_mistakes: Heel lifting off the floor.
Crashing the back knee down.
Knee caving inward under load.

exercises.name: Bear Crawl
exercises.summary: Crawl on hands and toes with knees hovering — a full-body anti-rotation drill that doubles as conditioning.
exercises.video_title: Bear Crawl Exercise Tutorial - Proper Form and Technique
instructions: Set up on hands and toes, knees an inch off the floor and under your hips, back flat.
Move the opposite hand and foot together a small step forward.
Keep your hips low and level — no swaying side to side. Crawl forward, then back.
form_tips: Imagine balancing a cup of water on your lower back.
Small steps keep it controlled.
Wrists under shoulders, weight spread across the whole hand.
common_mistakes: Hips rocking side to side.
Butt piking up toward the ceiling.
Big lunging steps that break the control.

exercises.name: Forward Lunge
exercises.summary: Step forward into the lunge — a little more demanding to control than the reverse version.
exercises.video_title: How To Do A Forward Lunge | Exercise Demonstration
instructions: Stand tall, hands on your hips, core braced.
Step one foot forward and bend both knees toward 90 degrees.
Keep your front knee over your ankle and your torso upright.
Push back through the front foot to return to standing, then alternate.
form_tips: Take a long enough step that the front shin stays near vertical.
Lower with control — don't fall into the bottom.
Look ahead for balance.
common_mistakes: Front knee jamming far past the toes.
Torso pitching forward.
Front knee caving inward.

exercises.name: Lateral Lunge
exercises.summary: Step out to the side and sit into one hip — trains a direction most programs ignore.
exercises.video_title: How To Series | Lateral Lunge
instructions: Stand tall, then take a wide step directly out to one side.
Sit back and down into that hip, bending the knee, keeping the other leg straight.
Both feet point forward; keep your chest up.
Push back to standing and repeat, or alternate sides.
form_tips: Push your hips back as you bend the working knee.
Keep the straight leg's foot flat on the floor.
Only go as deep as you can keep a flat back.
common_mistakes: Working knee travelling past the toes.
Rounding the back to reach lower.
Feet turning out instead of pointing forward.

exercises.name: Curtsy Lunge
exercises.summary: Step one leg diagonally behind the other — great for the side-glutes and hip control.
exercises.video_title: Curtsy Lunge. Proper form and technique tutorial.
instructions: Stand tall, then step one foot back and across behind the other into a 'curtsy'.
Bend both knees, keeping your front knee tracking over your shoes.
Keep your chest lifted and hips facing forward.
Push through the front foot to return, then alternate sides.
form_tips: Keep your hips square — resist the twist.
Most of the weight stays on the front leg.
Go slow; the crossover challenges balance.
common_mistakes: Hips rotating open toward the back leg.
Front knee caving inward.
Leaning the torso forward.

exercises.name: Jumping Lunge
exercises.summary: Explode out of a lunge and switch legs mid-air — power and conditioning in one.
exercises.video_title: How to do a Lunge Jump | Proper Form & Technique | NASM
instructions: Start in a split stance, both knees bent toward 90 degrees.
Drive up explosively and switch your legs in the air.
Land softly back in a lunge on the other side and immediately absorb into the next rep.
form_tips: Land quiet with the front shin near vertical.
Keep your torso upright the whole time.
Master reverse lunges and split squats before adding the jump.
common_mistakes: Front knee slamming forward on the landing.
Landing stiff-legged.
Losing the upright torso mid-air.

exercises.name: Step-Up
exercises.summary: Step onto a sturdy chair or box one leg at a time — simple, scalable single-leg strength.
exercises.video_title: Step Up Tutorial - Proper Form and Technique
instructions: Stand facing a knee-height sturdy box, bench or bottom stair.
Place one whole foot on the surface and drive through that heel to stand up on it.
Step back down softly with control. Finish reps, then switch legs.
form_tips: Drive through the heel of the top foot to load the glute.
Minimise the push-off from the bottom foot.
Lower a higher step to regress, raise it to progress.
common_mistakes: Pushing hard off the trailing foot.
Letting the top knee cave inward.
Bouncing off the bottom.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Glute Bridge
exercises.summary: A glute bridge on one leg — twice the load and a check on side-to-side balance.
exercises.video_title: Single Leg Glute Bridge Tutorial - Proper Form and Technique
instructions: Lie on your back, one knee bent with the foot flat, the other leg extended.
Press your ribs down and brace your core.
Drive through the planted heel to lift your hips until your body is straight from knee to shoulder.
Squeeze the glute at the top, then lower with control. Finish reps, then switch.
form_tips: Keep your hips level — don't let one side drop.
Push the movement with your glute, not your lower back.
Pause and squeeze for a beat each rep.
common_mistakes: Hips tilting or twisting.
Arching the back to finish the lift.
Pushing through the toes instead of the heel.

exercises.name: Frog Pump
exercises.summary: A bridge with soles of the feet together — one of the best pure glute-activation drills.
exercises.video_title: How To Do A Frog Pump Glute Bridge
instructions: Lie on your back, press the soles of your feet together and let your knees fall open.
Pull your heels in toward your body.
Press through the outer edges of your feet and squeeze your glutes to lift your hips.
Hold the squeeze for a beat, then lower.
form_tips: Keep the range small — it's all about the glute squeeze.
Ribs stay down; don't arch the back.
Do these as a warm-up before squats and hinges.
common_mistakes: Arching the lower back instead of squeezing the glutes.
Letting the knees drift up instead of open.
Rushing the reps.

exercises.name: Band Hip Thrust
exercises.summary: A shoulders-elevated hip thrust with a loop band over the hips — the most direct glute builder at home.
exercises.video_title: Hip Thrust Tutorial – Proper Form and Technique
instructions: Sit with your upper back against a couch or bench, a loop band over your hips and pinned under your hands.
Plant your feet flat, shins vertical at the top.
Drive through your heels and push your hips up until your body is flat from knees to shoulders.
Squeeze your glutes hard at the top, then lower with control.
form_tips: Tuck your chin and keep your ribs down — squeeze, don't arch.
Pause at the top of every rep.
Push a mini band around the knees too, to fight the knees caving in.
common_mistakes: Over-arching the lower back at the top.
Feet too far forward so the hamstrings take over.
Only pushing halfway up.

exercises.name: Band Donkey Kick
exercises.summary: A kneeling glute isolation with a band around the knees — pure burn, joint-friendly.
exercises.video_title: How to Do Donkey Kicks with Resistance Bands
instructions: Get on all fours with a loop band around your legs just above the knees, back flat.
Keeping one knee bent at 90 degrees, press that foot toward the ceiling.
Stop when your thigh is in line with your torso — no higher.
Lower slowly against the band. Finish reps, then switch.
form_tips: Keep your core tight and back neutral — don't arch to lift higher.
Squeeze the glute at the top.
Control the way down; don't let the band snap the leg back.
common_mistakes: Kicking so high the lower back arches.
Rotating the hips open.
Using momentum instead of the glute.

exercises.name: B-Stance Romanian Deadlift
